title: Agentic Speed, Human Control: How a 20+ year game dev is vibecoding.
author: shiny_guruw
selftext:
I've been making games on and off for about 20 years, both professionally and as a hobby. The massive amount of "I one shot a game with claude" posts that hit my feed inspired me to run a little experiment in vibecoding.

The video is a game Claude Opus 5.5 made in about 3 hours following an opinionated architecture I laid out for it. I wrote up a blog on my site where I share the methodology and the prompts I used.  
  
Writeup: [https://lioralabs.dev/blog/agentic-speed-human-control](https://lioralabs.dev/blog/agentic-speed-human-control)

Play for free: [https://shiny-guru.itch.io/gravewake](https://shiny-guru.itch.io/gravewake)

Source: [https://github.com/LioraLabs/gravewake](https://github.com/LioraLabs/gravewake)

comments.author: cxfoulke
comments.body:
Could you of not vibe coded your write up its painful to llm speech for more than 10 seconds. 

I also feel like if you are making an article about how you do things... You should probably achieve something novel. This game could be replicated and made exactly by anyone on this sub. There no need for any layer of complexity. 

There are interesting problems to solve in "vibe coded" games  style consistency, effect creep, context bloat, testing bloat etc  

  
Also you've been making games for 20 years and you didnt add hit decent enemy hit feedback and a cooldown on the attack... I feel like 1 minute of prompting would make the combat feel way better.

replies.author: shiny_guruw
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback. Clearly the thesis of the article didn't come across. I am showcasing an approach to build a semantic layer between the agent and the human that lays out an architecture that both can work in.

The game is a throwaway experiment to showcase a possible framework for building games with AI.

replies.author: shiny_guruw
replies.body:
Partly. I would never say this is the only way to build games with AI. It's really just putting a couple of opinions I have to the test.

I do believe that without a clear vision of architecture, iteration will become impossible at some point. That's true of both human and agent development, though.

replies.author: kilographix
replies.body: Ive had success not oneshotting but building games in a few prompts with testing in between in a single html file. I think it is similar to what youre saying but i havent had issues with adjusting between stages without laying out the architecture ahead of time.

replies.author: Material-Database-24
replies.body:
With +20y in SWE I'd say the same. AI is still "bad" at architecture and vision for future improvements and/or features. If no human intervention is made, and more than one shot is used, the code starts to steer towards smelly.

And I think experienced humans are still better at it - we do it by intuition, think that "what if I need to do x, y and z here in future", and take that already into account while doing 1st iteration.
